observed_text:
After thorough cleaning, the registered inspection domains are: bearing raceways and external surfaces; cage wear; increase in internal clearance; degradation of tolerances; and other damage or abnormalities [EV-K01-010]. The additional context factors for considering reuse are the degree of bearing wear, the function of the machine, the importance of the bearing in the machine, operating conditions, and the time until the next inspection [EV-K01-010]. Smooth hand rotation alone would not approve reuse of this demonstration bearing: hand rotation is described only for small nonseparable ball bearings, separable and large bearings use different methods, and the card explicitly states it is not a complete reuse decision rule [EV-K01-010]. The caller-assigned class 'inner_race' and the scenario assumption of shaft/housing misalignment during mounting are teaching inputs, not observations or classifier inferences, and they do not establish actual damage cause or reuse [EV-K01-010].

Evidence limitations:
The card is generic bearing education only; it is not a complete reuse or rejection rule and must not alone decide reuse, replacement, or release [EV-K01-010].
Hand rotation is valid only for small nonseparable ball bearings; separable and large bearing methods differ and must not be generalized [EV-K01-010].
No model-specific thresholds, actual device records, sampling quantity, or aviation/reuse authorization were supplied [EV-K01-010].
The 'inner_race' class and the misalignment scenario assumption are caller-specified teaching inputs, not source-proven sample facts or inferred damage causes [EV-K01-010].
